standoff_budget.method: sw_common.standoff_table: an object painted on a surface at stand-off s slides from its true place by the angle between the eye's rays to the object and to the point where the render camera's ray through it meets the surface; the budget is the greatest s that keeps the slide within N pixels of a 2560 x 1440 frame, the smallest over STREET_SQUARE, STREET_30 and CLOSE_35 and their mirror images

standoff_rules_m.derivation: true (20 px): back wall 0.33, sides 0.06, floor/ceiling 0.03; tolerated (40 px): back wall 0.64, sides 0.11, floor/ceiling 0.06; the rules are those figures rounded down to 5 mm and to the nearest builder-friendly depth: a shelf (0.30) is true, a counter or machine against the back wall (0.60) is tolerated, a side wall carries only boards and 0.10 racks, the floor only flat things

resolution.what: screen pixels per picture texel over the glass area at the game's 1440 lines (more than 2 is soft)
resolution.reading: at 4096 wide the picture is never softer than 1.2 screen pixels a texel from 0.5 m; at 2048 it is soft over 13 per cent of the glass at 0.5 m and 4 per cent at 1.5 m: the picture is made 4096 wide

window_far_end_angle_deg.reading: the angle off the glass normal at which the window's far end is seen from a pavement point 35 degrees off the window centre: at 1.5 m it is 61 degrees, where the research puts the glass's own Fresnel hand-over (about 60); nearer than 1.5 m part of the window is in the hand-over and the review would judge the glass, which is the game's, not the room

slide_px_at_2560x1440.reading: the same object slides by about the same number of pixels from 0.5 to 1.9 m (the angle sets it, not the distance): the 20 px line is held by back-wall shelf goods and flat boards at the CLOSE camera, a counter against the back wall is tolerated, a free item or a deep side unit is not

honest_range.why: the method holds from the far pavement (8.75 m) and from the near pavement down to 1.5 m from the glass at 35 degrees, with 4096-wide pictures and the stand-off rules: there the room's surfaces are sharp (median 0.50 screen pixel a texel at 4096), back-wall stock 0.25 deep slides 3 to 15 px, a 0.05 board 5 to 15 px, a floor item 0.03 high 4 to 22 px (so the floor's rule is 0.025), and the whole window is seen at under 62 degrees. Nearer than 1.5 m the window's far end passes 62 degrees (67 at 1.0 m, 76 at 0.5 m), where the glass's own Fresnel takes over, so part of every nearer view is the glass's and the display's, not the room's. The near 0.55 m is therefore real geometry, and the review's CLOSE view stands at 1.5 m.

gate_in_the_cloud.how: The builder shows what the game will show without Unreal: the shop's front is assembled in Blender from the 3.2 parts (and the door and lobby of this target), the display's real meshes stand in front of the card where the display is, and the card is a flat quad with an emission picture computed PER CAMERA by tools/ue/make_interior_material.py's `trace` (the Python function, imported, not rewritten): for every pixel of the card the card point and the eye go through `trace` and the picture is sampled at the returned (u, v), bilinear with mips, times the state's brightness (day 0.15, night 0.7). That picture is baked to an image for the camera and set as the card's emission in Cycles, so what is judged is the game's rule pixel for pixel; the glass is the game's job and is left out (a clear 6 mm pane with no reflection) or drawn at the game's day value only if the review asks.
gate_in_the_cloud.check: PRJ-03: the baked card picture equals the trace-sampled picture for the same camera to within 1 level
gate_in_the_cloud.views: per shop: STREET_SQUARE, STREET_30, CLOSE_35, by day and by night (six renders); the review of two views is STREET and CLOSE
gate_in_the_cloud.what_it_cannot_show: the game's glass reflections, Lumen's light on the display, the card's motion vectors under TSR, the exposure: those stay owed on the PC

inventory.rule: every model a build places is listed in its inventory.json; each must be in `polyhaven`, `scripted` or a Sketchfab uid of `sketchfab_checked`; none in `denied`; no object, material or text contains a word of the blocklists; every Poly Haven model's 1k maps are looked at BEFORE the build (step 0) and every maker's mark is painted out of its base-colour map exactly as that model's `blank` step says (`texture_marks`); the gate then tests the listed boxes and the builder looks at the final map (INV-06); the approved pawnbroker pictures are searched by eye at full size for the same marks (INV-05)

texture_marks.step: script step (one per listed map, before the model is placed): open the map; for each box, take the fill (the median colour of a 6 px ring just outside the box, the sampled value is given for reference), paint the whole box to it, then copy a same-size patch of the map's own grain from the nearest clean area over it (no flat patch); write <map>_clean.jpg beside it; point the glTF material's baseColorTexture at the clean map. 'Whole label area' means every box listed for that map. The normal and roughness maps are not touched (a print has no relief at 1k).

final_check.script: after the step, for each listed box of the FINAL texture: the largest difference from the ring colour on any channel is at most 24 levels and fewer than 2 per cent of the box's pixels have a gradient above 40 levels: an erased box is the ring colour plus grain, with no glyph edge in it; a box that fails fails the build; where a whole map is replaced (boxes [0, 0, 1024, 1024]: cigarette_pack, the picture frames' artworks) the script checks that the final map is a different file from the downloaded one (its hash differs) and that the glTF points at the project's print
final_check.visual: the builder opens the final map at 100 per cent beside the original and reads every printed word (a mark outside the listed boxes, a half-erased glyph and a seam are what no script can test); any word, number, logo, face or sticker still legible is a fault, and a new mark found goes into this list with its box

texture_marks.map_frame: pixels of the model's 1k glTF base-colour map, 1024 x 1024, origin top left, [x0, y0, x1, y1]
texture_marks.looked_at: all 104 models' 1k base-colour maps on 12 October after the review (25 contact sheets at 512 px; the marked ones at 1k with the boxes drawn on them); thumbnails alone had missed 'Dixons'
texture_marks.the_approved_pictures: pawnbroker_day.png, _night_lit.png, _night_dark.png (approved 6 October) were made with cassette_player and Camera_01 among the stock: the builder reads their back walls at full size for the marks above (could_not_settle, first item)
